headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,510 AS TREASURY BUYBACK CRUSHES LONG YIELDS — FRESH 6-WEEK HIGH ONE DAY AFTER FOMC MINUTES
snippet: Gold traded at $4,510.66 per ounce in early U.S. hours on Thursday August 20 — a fresh six-week high — extending Wednesday's 4.13% Treasury buyback rally that pushed the metal from $4,313 to $4,512 on the day the July FOMC minutes revealed the most divided Fed vote since 2016. September rate-hike odds have collapsed from roughly 60% earlier this month to 31% after soft payrolls, CPI, and PPI prints, and the entire advance now hinges on whether Chair Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole keynote validates or reverses that market-priced hold. Gold is up more than 10% in August alone, its best monthly gain since January, and the technical setup ($4,500 held above the 2026 high on the day-close) puts the metal in position to test $4,600 into the Jackson Hole window.

headline: TROILUS DRILLS 8.84 g/t AuEq OVER 4.8m — Z87 HIGH-GRADE MINERALIZATION EXTENDS 400m BEYOND CURRENT PIT SHELL IN QUEBEC
snippet: Troilus Mining Corp. (TSX: TLG) announced August 20 results from five drill holes totaling 2,915 metres at the Z87 extension of its gold-copper Troilus Project in north-central Quebec, highlighted by 8.84 g/t AuEq over 4.8 metres. All five holes were extensions of existing drill holes originating from the J Zone, designed to test the down-plunge continuity of high-grade Z87 mineralization beyond the current resource — one hole extended known mineralization 400 metres beyond the existing pit shell. The development plan has evolved from an underground concept beneath the historic J and Z87 pits into a 50,000-tonne-per-day open-pit operation, and every high-grade extension hole beyond the current pit shell directly expands the resource envelope that will underpin the coming feasibility work.

headline: OSISKO METALS HITS 312m AT 0.56% Cu AT GASPÉ — 15 NEW HOLES, 35 INTERCEPTS DRIVE MRE UPGRADE AT PAST-PRODUCING QUEBEC MINE
snippet: Osisko Metals Inc. (TSX: OM) released August 20 results from the 2026 drill program at the past-producing Gaspé Copper Project in Québec, including 312 metres averaging 0.56% Cu among 35 mineralized intercepts from 15 new drill holes. Results are categorized as either infill intercepts inside the 2026 MRE model — designed to upgrade Inferred resources to Measured or Indicated — or expansion intercepts outside the model that could add in-pit or out-of-pit tonnage. Osisko acquired 100% of the Murdochville-area mine from Glencore Canada in July 2023, and with LME copper cash-to-3M spreads still trading at historically wide levels and Comex holding above $6.40/lb, restart economics for a past-producing brownfield copper asset at scale are as favourable as they have been in a decade.

headline: SIRIOS INTERSECTS 2.4 g/t Au OVER 48.5m AT CHEECHOO — VISIBLE GOLD IN 8 HOLES, RESOURCE UPDATE DUE POST-PHASE 1
snippet: Sirios Resources Inc. (TSXV: SOI) announced August 20 assay results from the first five holes (1,753 metres) of Phase 1 drilling at the Cheechoo gold project in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Québec, highlighted by 2.4 g/t Au over 48.5 metres and visible gold in eight drill holes to date. The summer 2026 program has completed 33 holes for 13,555 metres with four rigs active, with CEO Jean-Félix Lepage stating the preliminary results support the thesis that Cheechoo's resource can grow meaningfully beyond the 2025 estimate of 35 Mt at 1.12 g/t indicated (1,262 koz) plus 42.7 Mt at 1.23 g/t inferred (1,688 koz). Phase 1 is on track to wrap in September ahead of an updated resource estimate — a hard catalyst on the calendar with an active drill program compounding into it.

headline: UR-ENERGY SHIPS FIRST URANIUM FROM SHIRLEY BASIN — 2nd WYOMING ISR MINE ONLINE, 4.2M lb COMBINED CAPACITY NOW LICENSED
snippet: Ur-Energy Inc. (NYSE American: URG) announced August 19 the first shipment of uranium from its Shirley Basin in-situ recovery mine to the Lost Creek processing plant in Wyoming, marking the company's formal transition to a multi-asset domestic U.S. producer. Shirley Basin — which moved from construction decision to production in just 2.5 years — holds licensed wellfield and toll-processing capacity of 2.0 million pounds U3O8 equivalent annually, bringing Ur-Energy's combined licensed capacity across Lost Creek and Shirley Basin to 4.2 million pounds. With spot uranium at $88/lb and utilities returning to term contracting at $75–85/lb, a permitted, funded, and now producing second ISR mine in Wyoming is a rare execution milestone for a small-cap U.S. uranium producer — the kind of transition Sprott and other sector allocators reward with multiple expansion.

headline: COPPER RETREATS FROM RECORDS AS LME INVENTORIES REBUILD — TRAFIGURA-LED 20,000-TON INFLOW LARGEST DAILY BUILD SINCE APRIL
snippet: LME three-month copper fell to $13,888 per tonne — a two-week low — extending a three-day decline as a fresh 20,000-tonne warehouse inflow (the biggest daily build since April, largely delivered by Trafigura) began to ease the historic physical squeeze that had pushed the cash-to-three-month spread to $553/t on August 17, the widest since 2021. The LME had introduced emergency measures on August 14 to cap further spot spikes, and the pullback in prices confirms those measures — combined with real physical delivery response — are functioning. For TSX-V copper juniors, the structural take-away is unchanged: even with a modest inventory rebuild, benchmark copper still trades within striking distance of all-time highs on tight forward supply and accelerating grid/AI-driven demand.

headline: SILVER RIPS TO $68.11 — 7.5% ONE-DAY REBOUND FROM WEDNESDAY'S $63 LOW AS YIELDS COLLAPSE AND GOLD-SILVER RATIO NARROWS
snippet: Silver traded at $68.11 per troy ounce Thursday morning August 20 — a roughly 7.5% bounce off Wednesday's session low of $63.10 — as the Treasury buyback that drove gold to fresh six-week highs pulled real yields sharply lower and reignited the industrial-and-monetary bid for silver. Silver is now up nearly 14% in August, still outrunning gold's 10% August gain on a percentage basis, and the sharp one-day snap-back after Wednesday's mid-day divergence suggests the underlying industrial demand thesis — solar, EVs, grid electronics — is still absorbing supply on any dip. The gold-silver ratio compressed to roughly 66:1 from Wednesday's high of 71:1, a mean-reversion move consistent with a broader precious-metals uplift rather than a narrow gold-only rally.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER HITS 13.12% CuEq AT MINTO — PHASE 2 DRILLING KEEPS EXPANDING YUKON POLYMETALLIC ZONE
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSXV: SKRK) reported additional Phase 2 drill results August 20 from the Minto Project in Yukon, including a hole grading 13.12% copper equivalent — a high-grade polymetallic intercept that continues to expand the known zones with strong copper-gold-silver credits. Minto is a past-producing property with brownfield infrastructure in a jurisdiction that offers permitting advantages relative to most Latin American copper camps. A double-digit CuEq hit at a permitted brownfield site with existing mill, camp, and road access is a rare risk-return profile in copper right now — one that directly ties into the same physical supply story driving LME spreads and TSX-V explorer multiples across the sector.

headline: ANGLO-TECK $53B MERGER AWAITS CHINA AND KOREA APPROVAL — CLOSING WINDOW SLIPS TO SEPTEMBER 2026-MARCH 2027
snippet: The $53-billion all-stock Anglo American / Teck Resources merger — voted through by 99%+ of Anglo shareholders in December 2025 and cleared under the Investment Canada Act on December 16, 2025 — is now waiting on clearances from China and South Korea, with the projected closing window now sitting between September 2026 and March 2027. Anglo CEO Duncan Wanblad said the company is actively engaged with Chinese regulators though specifics have not been disclosed. Once closed, Anglo Teck will rank among the top five global copper producers at an annual output of roughly 1.35 million tonnes, a scale that will make the combined entity a natural strategic buyer of the next generation of copper juniors — from BC porphyry discoveries to Chilean brownfield restarts. The extended review window is itself a signal that critical-mineral M&A is no longer a routine antitrust exercise.

headline: BUSINESS STANDARD: CAN THE AUGUST GOLD RALLY SURVIVE JACKSON HOLE? — WARSH'S FIRST KEYNOTE IS THE ONLY SCHEDULED EVENT THAT CAN REVERSE IT
snippet: Business Standard's August 19 gold outlook piece frames the coming week starkly: gold's entire 10% August advance rests on the collapse in September rate-hike odds from 50% to 31% following three soft data prints (jobs, CPI, PPI), and the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (August 27-29) — headlined by Chair Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed chair on August 28 — is the only scheduled event capable of reversing those expectations. If Warsh validates the market-priced hold, the piece argues gold's technical breakout above $4,500 is set to run toward $4,600+; if he re-anchors the September FOMC toward a hike, the sharp reversal from a crowded speculative long position could compress the sector's newfound retail flows into GDX/GDXJ as quickly as they arrived. For miners, the leverage is asymmetric in both directions.
